DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http•.//www dilg.com.ph OILG OPINION NO. 44 07 AUG 2019 S. 200 HON. CHERADEE A. BELIGAN Acting Vice Mayor Municipality of Rizal Province of Kalinga Dear Acting Vice Mayor Beligan: This has reference to your letter dated 01 April 2019 requesting for legal opinion relative to the veto power of the Governor over review of Municipal Appropriation Ordinance by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. In your letter, the facts are as follows: On November 8, 2018, the Sanggunian Bayan (SB) of Rizal in the province of Kalinga passed Appropriation Ordinances (AOs) on the annual budget of the municipality and the annual budget of the Local Economic Enterprises for fiscal year 2019; On December 5, 2018, the AOs were transmitted to the Office of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) for review; On January 29, 2019, the SP approved the AOs through SP Resolution No. 2019-05 (SP Resolution 2019-05); On March 11, 2019, SP Resolution 2019-05 was transmitted to the Office of the Governor; Governor Joel C. Baac of the Provincial Government of Kalinga vetoed the SP Resolution 2019-05 on the grounds, to wit: a. b. c. The Appropriation Ordinance does not contain any appropriation for Gender-and- Development-related projects, which runs contrary to Joint Memorandum Circular No. 20126-1 entitled "Amendments to PCW-DILG-DB,-NEDA JMC No. 2013-01: Guidelines on the Localization of the Magna Carta for Women"; There exists no indication that the Intelligence Fund that was advanced for the previous year is fully liquidated, which raises the presumption that such missing funds or property was put to personal use; and There is no funding for the creation and operation of Municipal Solid Waste Management Board as mandated by Republic Act No. 9003, otherwise known as the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.

The questions/issues are hereunder quoted in verbatim: I. Whether the veto message of the Honorable Governor is in place, provided that the reasons stated therein have been complied 2. Whether or not resolution of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan is subject to the exercise of veto power of the Governor 3. In case the veto power is not in order, does the Honorable Governor can be charged administratively on his actions? 4. Lastly, can the Local Government Unit of Rizal, Kalinga implement the Appropriation Ordinances authorizing the Annual Budget of the municipality and the operating budget ofthe LEE for FY 2019, provided the LFC of the Province and the Sangguniang Panlalawigan already reviewed and approved the same? It is the understanding of this level that, ultimately, the aforementioned questions hinge on the issue of whether or not the SP resolution reviewing the component municipality's ordinance is subject to the approval of the Governor. We find Section 56 and 327 of RA 7160 applicable. They state, respectively: Section 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panna wigan. (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sanggunian panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies ofapproved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days aher the receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to theprovincial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period of ten (IO) days from receipt of the documents, inform the sangguniang panlalawigan in writing ofhis comments or recommendations, which may be considered by the sangguniang panlala wigan in making its decision. (c) If the sangguniang panlalawigan finds that such an ordinance or resolution is beyond the power conferred upon the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned, it shall declare such ordinance or resolution invalid in whole or in part. The sangguniang panlalawigan shall enter its action in the minutes and shall advise the corresponding city or municipal authorities of the action it has taken.

(d) If no action has been taken by the sangguniang panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission of such an ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. Section 327. Revléw of Appropriation Ordinances of Component Cities and Municipalities. - The sangguniangpanlalawigan shall review the ordinance authorizing annual or supplemental appropriations of component cities and municipalities in the same manner and within the same period prescribed for the review ofother ordinances. If within ninety (90) days from receipt of copies of such ordinance, the sangguniang panlalawigan takes no action thereon, the same shall be deemed to have been reviewed in accordance with law and shall continue to be in full force and effect. If within the same period, the sangguniang panna wigan shall have ascertained that the ordinance authorizing annual or supplemental appropriations has not complied with the requirements set forth in this Title, the sangguniangpanla/awigan shall, within the ninety- day period hereinabove prescribed declare such ordinance inoperative in its entirety or in part. Items of appropriation contrary to limitations prescribed in this Title or in excess of the amounts prescribed herein shall be disallowed or reduced accordingly. The sangguniang panlalawigan shall within the same period advise the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned through the local chief executive of any action on the ordinance under revl&vv. Upon receipt of such advice, the city or municipal treasurer concerned shall not make further disbursements of funds from any of the items ofappropriation declared inoperative, disallowed or reduced. In view of the foregoing, it is the Sangguniang Panlalawigan that has the express authority to review the Appropriation Ordinance of the respective component city or municipality. The law does not specify nor imply that the same shall be presented to the Governor for approval. Thus, in our view, the said review is an action that only SP may take. To emphasize, Section 56 (b) and (c), as aforecited, expressly provides that the review of the ordinance of the component city/municipality starts upon the examination of the SP or its transmittal to the provincial attorney or, in his/her absence, the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. Thereafter, the SP considers the review of the provincial attorney or the provincial prosecutor before it declares such ordinance invalid in whole or in part. Verily, the SP is even the one mandated to advise the SB concerned through the local chief executive of any action on the ordinance under review. In addition, what is clear in RA 7160 is the necessity of the presentation of every ordinance enacted to the provincial governor or city or municipal mayor for approval.l But it is not clear if it is the same with resolutions. In our previous opinion, we state; " Section 54. Approval of Ordinances. -

this Department consistently opines that not all legislative measures passed by the Sangguniang Bayan should be subject to the approval or veto of the Municipal Mayor. The scope of the approval or veto power of the local chief executive is limited only to (I) ordinances, and (2) resolutions approving local development plans and public investment programs. Allow us to explain our legal basis thereto. Section 54 of the Local Government Code of 1991 is explicit that every ordinance shall be subject to the approval of the local chief executive but it seems uncertain in the case of resolutions. No mention was made with respect to resolutions but the third sentence of the same section authorizes the sanggunian concerned to override the veto of the governor or mayor "thereby making the ordinance or resolution effective. " Let it be noted that where the veto power is exercisable, as an alternative, the approval of the measure is also required. "2 Accordingly, it is our view that the SP resolution reviewing the component municipality's AO is not subject to the approval of the Governor. Verily, the veto shall not be made applicable to a legislative measure that is not subject to the Governor's approval in the first place. Such being the case, the SP Resolution declaring the AO on the annual budget and AO on annual budget of its local economic enterprise for FY 2019 inoperative in part and operative in its entirety, respectively, shall guide the Sangguniang Bayan on their implementation of the same - not making any further disbursements of funds from any items of appropriation declared inoperative, disallowed, or reduced, provided that the SP advises SB of its action. Although to our understanding, the failure of the SP to advise SB of its action does not result to AO being deemed reviewed in accordance with law and to continue in full force and effect because we considered that SP here had taken action. This Department had consistently opined that the phrase "take action" should be construed as either approval or disapproval of the ordinance and not just any other action of the reviewing sanggunian, such as referral to the committee.3 Again, SP in this case issued resolution declaring the subject AOs inoperative in part and operative in its entirety. We view that this is an application of the term "take action" referred to in the review of ordinances. We reiterate, nonetheless, the duty of the SP, as stated in the last paragraph of Section (a) Every ordinance enacted by the sangguniang panlala wigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sangguniang bayan shall be presented to theprovincialgovernororcityor municipal mayor, as the case may be. Ifthe local chiefexecutive concerned approves the same, he shall affix his signature on each and every page thereof; otherwise, he shall veto it and return the same with his objections to the sanggunian, which may proceed to reconsider the same. The sangunian concerned may override the veto of the local chief executive by two-thirds (2/3) vote ofall its members, thereby making the ordinance or resolution effective for all legal intents and purposes. (b) The veto shall be communicated by the local chief executive concerned to the sanggunian within fifteen (15) days in the case 0fa province, and ten (IO) days in the case ofa City Or a municipality; otherwise, the ordinance shall deemed approved as if he had signed it. (c) Ordinances enactea' by the sangguniang barangay shall, upon approval by the majority Of all its members, be Signed by thepunong barangay. (Sec. 54, RA 7160) 2 DILG Legal Opinion No. 27, s. 2010, 09 March 2010 3 DILG Legal Opinion No. 057-18 dated 22 August 2018

327, to advise the SB concerned through the local chief executive of the action taken on the ordinance under review within the same period within which SP shall take an action thereon i.e. 90 days from receipt of the ordinance. (Emphasis supplied). On the third query, if it can be proven that there is abuse of authority and not a mere mistake on the part of the Governor in vetoing a legislative measure not needing his approval, then he may be administratively liable. However, we herein note that, in this case, the Governor is incorrect to act upon a matter within the authority of the Sanggunian and that the SP is also mistaken in transmitting to him the issued resolution, when it is expressly obligated by law to advise the concerned SB, through the local chief executive, of its action, within the above- mentioned period. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Very truly yours, By the authority of the Secretary MARIVEL C.
